ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009; Companies Act 1993, Part 6A (ss 198A-198N) and the Companies (Ultimate Shareholder Information) Regulations 2022; Financial Transactions Reporting Regulations 2011; United Nations Act 1946 sanctions designations; and Russia Sanctions Act 2022.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille only: issue original certificate in New Zealand, then obtain apostille from the New Zealand Department of Internal Affairs Authentications Unit; do not chain consular legalization because New Zealand is a member of the Hague Apostille Convention.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille only: certified copy issued by the New Zealand Companies Office, followed by an apostille from the New Zealand Department of Internal Affairs Authentications Unit; consular legalization is not required and must not be added.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Incorporator and directors appearing before a New Zealand notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille only: notarization in New Zealand, then apostille by the New Zealand Department of Internal Affairs Authentications Unit; no consular legalization is applicable for apostille-convention member states.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Incorporator and first director or shareholder of the New Zealand Limited
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille only: certified true copy notarized by a New Zealand notary public, then apostilled by the New Zealand Department of Internal Affairs; consular legalization is mutually exclusive and shall not be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registered bank in New Zealand under the Banking Prudential Supervision Act 1989
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille only: bank letter signed by an authorized bank officer, notarized by a New Zealand notary public, then apostilled by the Department of Internal Affairs; consular legalization does not apply to apostille-convention signatory states.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Ultimate Shareholder Register and AML/CFT Compliance Certificate
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: New Zealand corporate counsel and the company's AML/CFT compliance officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille only: notarized certification of the ultimate shareholder register and AML/CFT compliance pack, followed by apostille through the Department of Internal Affairs; no consular legalization step is permitted.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Prior to incorporation, each director, ultimate shareholder, senior manager and authorized signatory of the New Zealand Limited must be screened against the New Zealand Financial Intelligence Unit designated persons list, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, and applicable New Zealand sanctions regimes. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for any domestic or foreign politically exposed person (PEP), requiring source of funds and source of wealth analysis, senior-management approval and ongoing transaction monitoring. All screening records, date-stamped with the screening vendor and version number, must be retained for at least five years under the AML/CFT Act 2009.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Register Name Availability Check (New Zealand Companies Office, companiesoffice.govt.nz)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory names must be in Latin script in English or te reo Maori; Chinese characters and non-Latin scripts are not accepted until a phonetic Latin-script transliteration is provided. The four-tier naming doctrine requires (1) a distinctive root, (2) a business or descriptive descriptor, (3) the mandatory legal-form suffix 'Limited' or 'Ltd', and (4) a compliance tag confirming any restricted or sensitive token has received the required prior approval from the relevant New Zealand regulator.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the New Zealand Companies Office issues a notice of refusal, the applicant must file a written appeal within 10 working days through the Companies Register objection channel, attaching the name search report, corrected four-tier naming analysis and, if applicable, prior written approval from the Ministry of Health, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment, or Reserve Bank of New Zealand. The Registrar will reconsider whether the name is identical or misleadingly similar to an existing registration and whether any prohibited token was used. If the objection is unsuccessful, the applicant may reserve a fresh name, and a current reservation can be renewed once for a further 20 working days; any final refusal may be challenged by judicial review in the High Court of New Zealand.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is acceptable as a New Zealand registered office only if it is a physical street address in New Zealand, open for service of process, and not a PO Box. However, for a certified Good Distribution Practice (GDP) pharmaceutical freight company, the Inland Revenue Department and New Zealand registered banks require actual commercial substance; a pure virtual office without qualified staff, lease documentation and GDP-compliant warehousing will likely be rejected for GST registration, customs clearance and bank account opening. The company must also maintain a separately licensed physical premises in New Zealand for pharmaceutical logistics activities.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Unannounced inspection checklist: front-door signage, staff availability during business hours, physical lease agreement, temperature-controlled pharma storage logs, chain-of-custody/GDP documentation, product recall and adverse-event records, Medsafe licence display and IRD GST records. Quantified risk: annual unannounced registry-site risk is low (5-10%); IRD and municipal compliance inspection risk is 15-25%; Medsafe and GDP on-site audit risk is 45-75% for active pharmaceutical logistics in the first year, escalating to over 80% if a virtual mailbox is used as the sole business address.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee: name search and reservation are free for 20 working days, with one renewal permitted.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market fixed fee for physical street address, mail receipt and service-of-process forwarding.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT UBO register build, PEP screening and GDP licensing pre-screen compliance pack
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External corporate counsel and AML/CFT consultant
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market fixed-fee arrangement for a low-risk standard entity, including Part 6A ultimate-shareholder register, sanctions screening and Medsafe GDP pre-screen checklist.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993, including sections 10 to 16 concerning company incorporation and registration, sections 27 to 36 concerning company constitutions, sections 45 to 50 concerning shares and shareholder liability, sections 128 to 138 concerning directors, sections 145 to 149 concerning directors duties and disclosure, and sections 189 to 193 concerning company records and accounting records. The Companies Act 1993 must be read with the Companies Regulations 1994 and the Companies Act 1993 fee regulations in force on the filing date.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies Office of the New Zealand Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment, acting through the New Zealand Companies Register.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for registration of a company under section 12 of the Companies Act 1993, submitted through the Companies Office online incorporation service, together with the required director, shareholder, registered office, address for service, and consent information.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: New Zealand has no statutory minimum issued or paid-up share capital for a limited company and no general statutory requirement to deposit subscription funds into an escrow account before incorporation. The company may be incorporated with one or more shares, provided that the application states the proposed share structure and the persons acquiring the shares. Shares should be issued for legally valid consideration and the company must maintain an accurate share register. Any unpaid amount on issued shares remains a liability of the relevant shareholder to the company. The Companies Office incorporation fee is prescribed in New Zealand dollars and the USD amount stated above is an indicative conversion only; the filing system charges the prescribed New Zealand dollar amount and may apply card or payment-provider fees.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: IT IS RESOLVED THAT: 1. The Company accepts the subscription by the subscriber named in the incorporation application for the number and class of ordinary shares stated in that application, each share ranking equally in respect of voting, dividend and distribution rights, and the consideration for those shares is approved as fully paid unless the share register records otherwise. 2. The registered office of the Company shall be the address stated in the incorporation application, and the address for service and communication address shall be maintained in accordance with the Companies Act 1993. 3. The Company shall adopt the constitution lodged with the Registrar, if any, and otherwise operate under the Companies Act 1993. 4. [Name] is appointed director, subject to the statutory consent and eligibility requirements, and [Name] is appointed company secretary, if the Board considers a secretary appropriate. 5. [Name] is authorised to open and operate the Company bank account, execute incorporation and banking documents, and complete all Companies Office, tax, licensing, insurance and regulatory registrations. 6. The officers shall establish the statutory registers, accounting records, health and safety controls, medicines compliance procedures and document retention system.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirm ownership, governance and regulated business perimeter
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Internal promoter and legal review, with Companies Office guidance where required
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm the proposed company name, share classes, subscriber, shareholders, directors, registered office, address for service, accounting basis, financial year end, beneficial ownership, and intended activities. Confirm that the business will provide freight forwarding, storage, distribution, validation, and related logistics services rather than manufacture or wholesale medicines unless the proposed activities require additional Medsafe licensing. Identify whether the company will possess, store, or transport prescription medicines, controlled drugs, dangerous goods, temperature-sensitive products, or clinical trial materials. Screen all directors and beneficial owners for statutory eligibility, sanctions, anti-money laundering, and conflict issues.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and name availability confirmation
Corporate structure chart and beneficial ownership statement
Passport or government identification for directors and shareholders
Residential addresses and service addresses for directors
Consent and eligibility confirmations for directors
Initial regulatory risk assessment for medicines, dangerous goods, privacy, employment and transport
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct the structure before filing, replace an ineligible director, revise the business description, or obtain a written regulatory interpretation from Medsafe, WorkSafe New Zealand, the relevant local authority, or a qualified New Zealand lawyer.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve and validate the company name
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Office online name reservation service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed name electronically and ensure that it is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name, does not breach statutory naming restrictions, and does not imply an unauthorised government, professional, financial, or regulated status. Reserve the name before filing the incorporation application and retain the reservation reference. The name should not misleadingly imply that the company is a pharmaceutical manufacturer, licensed wholesaler, clinical laboratory, or public authority if it will operate only as a logistics provider.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Submit an alternative name, remove restricted terminology, provide explanatory evidence if the Registrar queries the name, and refile within the reservation validity period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare a constitution if bespoke governance, reserved matters, share transfer restrictions, director appointment rights, deadlock rules, or investor protections are required. Otherwise, rely on the Companies Act 1993 default rules. Complete the application for registration with the company name, registered office, address for service, communication address, director particulars, shareholder particulars, share numbers and classes, and constitution election. The registered office and address for service must be physical New Zealand addresses capable of receiving documents during ordinary business hours; a post office box alone is insufficient. Obtain all required consents and signed authorisations before electronic submission.
required_dossiers: Director consent and certificate of eligibility
Registered office and address for service confirmation
Power of attorney or filing authority, if an agent files
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Amend the electronic application, upload corrected consent documents, address any statutory eligibility issue, and resubmit the queried particulars through the Companies Office portal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File incorporation application and pay prescribed fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed application electronically, pay the prescribed New Zealand dollar filing fee, and retain the transaction receipt and application reference. The filing agent must verify that all mandatory fields are consistent with the constitution, share subscription documents, and director consents. Do not represent the company as incorporated, enter contracts in its corporate name, or open a corporate bank account until the Registrar issues the certificate of incorporation, except under a properly documented pre-incorporation arrangement.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond promptly to a Companies Office requisition, correct the defective field or document, pay any additional fee, and resubmit. If registration is refused, obtain written reasons and seek administrative correction or legal advice on judicial review or other available relief.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receive certificate and establish statutory corporate records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Office and internal company records function
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Download and preserve the certificate of incorporation, company number, registration date, constitution, and Companies Register extract. Establish the share register, interests register, director register, minute book, written resolutions file, accounting records, contracts register, and statutory document retention schedule. Record the registered office, address for service, directors, shareholders, share classes, issue price, consideration, and allotment date. Ensure all corporate records are maintained in New Zealand or in a manner permitted by the Companies Act 1993 and are available for inspection where legally required.
required_dossiers: Registered office and address for service evidence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct inaccurate register information through the Companies Office change service, pass ratifying resolutions where appropriate, and maintain an audit trail explaining every correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pass initial board and shareholder resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company board and shareholders under the Companies Act 1993 and constitution
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting or circulate a written board resolution. Approve the share issue and consideration, adopt the registered office, appoint officers where applicable, approve banking mandates, appoint accountants and legal advisers, adopt signing authorities, approve the annual return calendar, and authorise tax and regulatory registrations. If the constitution or share issue requires shareholder approval, obtain a shareholder written resolution. Record director disclosure of interests and abstention from conflicted decisions. Approve a compliance framework covering medicines, GDP, health and safety, privacy, transport, insurance, complaints, recalls, deviations, and document control.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Ratify defective procedural steps where legally permissible, reconvene the board, obtain missing consents, correct the minutes, and seek advice before relying on any conflicted or unauthorised transaction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for tax, employer and financial reporting obligations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment, and Companies Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for an Inland Revenue number and register for goods and services tax if the taxable activity is expected to exceed the statutory threshold or voluntary registration is commercially justified. Register as an employer before paying employees and establish payroll, PAYE, KiwiSaver and employment record systems. Determine whether the company must file foreign investment, withholding tax, non-resident withholding tax, or transfer pricing information. Maintain accounting records and prepare annual returns and financial statements according to the company's size, constitution, ownership and statutory filing category.
required_dossiers: Goods and services tax analysis and election
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct registration data, make late filings with voluntary disclosure where appropriate, pay interest and penalties, and request remission or instalment arrangements where statutory criteria are met.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Medsafe, the New Zealand Medicines and Medical Devices Safety Authority, within the Ministry of Health
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Map every proposed service against the Medicines Act 1981 and Medicines Regulations 1984. If the company purchases, sells, supplies, or otherwise deals in medicines as a wholesaler, apply for a Licence to Sell Medicines by Wholesale before commencing that activity. If the company merely transports or stores medicines as a contracted logistics provider, obtain written regulatory confirmation on whether the contractual model constitutes sale or supply and implement customer licensing checks. Nominate a responsible quality contact, establish GDP procedures, qualify premises and vehicles, validate temperature controls, control access, manage deviations and complaints, and maintain recall and product traceability procedures.
required_dossiers: Medsafe wholesale licence application, if applicable
Premises layout and storage zoning plan
Quality manual and standard operating procedures
Supplier and customer licence verification procedure
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to Medsafe deficiencies with a corrective action plan, suspend the affected activity, provide additional evidence, request a pre-application meeting, and appeal or seek review of an adverse licensing decision where a statutory right exists.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Implement GDP logistics validation and transport controls
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Medsafe for medicine compliance, WorkSafe New Zealand for workplace safety, and the New Zealand Transport Agency for applicable transport requirements
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Create a risk-based Good Distribution Practice quality system covering receipt, quarantine, release, picking, packing, dispatch, returns, recalls, falsified products, temperature excursions, data integrity, subcontractors, cleaning, pest control, security, and change control. Validate refrigerated and ambient lanes using calibrated equipment, documented worst-case profiles, seasonal studies, alarm response, backup power, and excursion disposition. Ensure subcontracted carriers and warehouses are qualified by written quality agreements and audit rights. Determine whether dangerous goods, dry ice, lithium batteries, controlled drugs, or hazardous substances trigger additional packaging, training, signage, storage, emergency plan or transport requirements.
required_dossiers: Risk assessment and lane qualification plan
Quality agreements with carriers and warehouses
Deviation, CAPA, recall and complaint logs
Business continuity and disaster recovery plan
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Quarantine affected stock, investigate and document the deviation, notify the customer or regulator where required, implement CAPA, repeat validation, and suspend noncompliant subcontractors or routes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Secure premises, building, fire and workplace approvals
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Relevant territorial authority as building consent authority, Fire and Emergency New Zealand, WorkSafe New Zealand, and the relevant local authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm zoning and permitted-use status before signing the lease. Obtain building consent for alterations, racking, cold rooms, fire systems, structural changes, loading areas, or change of use where required. Obtain a code compliance certificate or other required completion approval. Arrange fire risk assessment, evacuation scheme or procedure, emergency lighting, alarm and suppression systems, hazardous substance controls, forklift segregation, racking load certification, pedestrian controls, ventilation, first aid, and worker training. Obtain a compliance schedule and annual building warrant of fitness where the building systems require them.
required_dossiers: Compliance schedule and building warrant of fitness records
Worker training and emergency drill records
WorkSafe notifications or approvals, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Stop use of the affected area, remedy building or fire defects, submit amended plans, request a site inspection, and appeal a territorial authority decision through the statutory building or resource consent process.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete environmental and local authority review
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Relevant territorial or regional council under the Resource Management Act 1991, and the Environmental Protection Authority for nationally significant proposals or hazardous substance functions within its jurisdiction
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Determine whether the proposed warehouse and logistics site requires resource consent for land use, traffic, noise, stormwater, wastewater, air discharge, hazardous substances, outdoor storage, refrigeration plant, generator use, or earthworks. A normal pharmaceutical freight and storage operation does not automatically require a full environmental impact assessment. Obtain written planning confirmation or resource consent before commencing a non-permitted activity. Establish spill response, waste segregation, licensed disposal, wastewater controls, refrigerant management, and emissions monitoring appropriate to the site and products.
required_dossiers: Noise and traffic assessment, if required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Amend the site or operating method, obtain retrospective consent only where legally available, lodge a formal consent application, respond to information requests, and appeal a council decision to the Environment Court where permitted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Launch readiness, inspections and continuing compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Office, Medsafe, Inland Revenue, local authority, WorkSafe New Zealand, Fire and Emergency New Zealand, and relevant customers or auditors
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete a documented pre-launch audit. Confirm that all corporate registrations, tax accounts, insurance, leases, permits, fire controls, building approvals, GDP procedures, calibration certificates, supplier qualifications, data protection controls, employment records, and customer contracts are complete. Do not commence regulated medicine wholesale, storage, or handling before the required licence, permit, or written regulatory determination is in place. Maintain annual return filings, director and shareholder changes, licence renewals, incident reporting, internal audits, management review, training refreshers, recall testing, equipment calibration, and records retention.
required_dossiers: Annual return and statutory filing calendar
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Suspend the affected operation, notify regulators and customers when required, implement CAPA, conduct an independent compliance review, and resume operations only after documented closure of critical findings.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Medsafe, the New Zealand Medicines and Medical Devices Safety Authority, within the Ministry of Health, for medicines licensing; the relevant territorial and regional councils for premises, land use, discharge and environmental consents; and WorkSafe New Zealand for workplace and hazardous substance controls.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licence to Sell Medicines by Wholesale, where the company purchases, sells, supplies, or otherwise deals in medicines as a wholesaler under the Medicines Act 1981 and Medicines Regulations 1984. A logistics-only operator may not require this licence if it does not sell or supply medicines, but the precise contractual and operational model should be confirmed with Medsafe before commencement.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority of New Zealand, with the relevant territorial or regional council acting as the primary consent authority for ordinary warehouse and logistics activities
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Normally exempt from a full environmental impact assessment for an ordinary existing pharmaceutical freight, storage, validation, or distribution warehouse, subject to confirmation that the activity is permitted under the applicable district and regional plans. Resource consent may be required for land use, building alterations, traffic, noise, stormwater, wastewater, air discharge, hazardous substances, earthworks, outdoor storage, or refrigeration systems. A full assessment of environmental effects and, in exceptional cases, a nationally significant proposal process may apply to major or sensitive developments.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No universal pharmaceutical logistics emission threshold applies solely because medicines are stored or transported. The operator must comply with applicable regional plan and resource consent limits for stormwater, trade waste, wastewater, noise, dust, odour, refrigerants and air discharges. Wastewater must not be discharged to a stormwater system and trade waste must comply with the relevant council or utility consent. Pharmaceutical, chemical, contaminated, clinical, hazardous and temperature-control wastes must be segregated, labelled, stored securely, tracked and transferred to appropriately authorised contractors. Volatile organic compound emissions, refrigerant releases, generator emissions and hazardous substance discharges must remain within applicable consent, national environmental standard and hazardous substance controls. Spill containment, incident notification, environmental monitoring and corrective action must be documented.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain building consent and any required code compliance certificate from the relevant territorial authority for structural works, racking, cold rooms, fire systems, loading areas and changes of use. Maintain a building warrant of fitness and compliance schedule where required. Complete fire risk assessment and evacuation arrangements, and coordinate with Fire and Emergency New Zealand where an approved evacuation scheme or fire system certification is required. Certify racking, mezzanines, loading equipment, refrigeration systems and structural loads through competent persons. Comply with the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 and applicable regulations, including hazardous substances, worker training, personal protective equipment, forklift controls, manual handling, emergency planning, first aid, incident notification and worker engagement. Obtain any required hazardous substance location, stationary container, certified handler, compliance certification, dangerous goods, or transport documentation before storing or moving relevant substances.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD), New Zealand; online portal myIR
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities deriving New Zealand-source income must first obtain a New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) via the Companies Office registration process or apply directly to the Inland Revenue using the applicable IRD number application form (e.g., IR 742 for non-individuals or the composite company registration process through the Companies Office). Upon approval, the entity is issued a unique IRD number or is linked to the existing NZBN-based registration, after which it must register for GST, employer obligations, and any industry-specific excise or levy regimes as applicable.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand permits a look-through company (LTC) election for qualifying close-held companies under Subpart HB of the Income Tax Act 2007, but does not operate a US-style check-the-box regime. Hybrid mismatch rules under Subpart FH may apply to cross-border arrangements, and an LTC election is irrevocable for the first five years.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST), a value-added tax
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 in taxable supplies over a 12-month rolling period; voluntary registration permitted below threshold
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, API-based pre-approval, or digital stamping mandate exists in New Zealand. Electronic invoicing is voluntary and primarily facilitated through the New Zealand Peppol e-Invoicing network. GST returns are filed electronically via myIR or approved software.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported from New Zealand within 28 days of the time of supply are zero-rated; services supplied to a non-resident who is outside New Zealand at the time of supply and not directly connected with New Zealand land or goods, or remote services consumed outside New Zealand, may also be zero-rated. The supplier must hold sufficient documentary evidence proving export and offshore consumption to support the zero-rating treatment.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (NZ Export Entry / Trade Single Window electronic declaration)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill
Customs-approved proof of export / port and voyage details
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank foreign exchange receipt evidence
Packing list and any applicable GDP / conformity certificates
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Inland Revenue and New Zealand Customs Service may audit export zero-rating claims. Incorrect zero-rating exposes the supplier to reassessment at the standard 15% GST rate, use-of-money interest from the original due date, and shortfall penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994: 20% for failing to take reasonable care, up to 150% for evasion or gross carelessness. Fraudulent export refunds can result in criminal prosecution and substantial financial penalties, with mandatory repayment of any GST refund plus penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua) — the sole central bank and prudential regulator of registered banks. New Zealand maintains no exchange control regime administered by the RBNZ; foreign exchange transactions are unrestricted. The Overseas Investment Office (OIO) administers the Overseas Investment Act 2005 for non-resident investment screening, while the Department of Internal Affairs (DIA) supervises AML/CFT compliance for conventional banks and the Financial Markets Authority (FMA) regulates non-bank financial services.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The New Zealand dollar (NZD) is a freely floating and fully convertible fiat currency with a liberalised capital and current account. There are no restrictions on the purchase or sale of foreign exchange, no surrender requirements, and no central bank licensing for FX transactions. Profit remittances from a non-resident-owned NZ Ltd are unrestricted, subject only to normal Non-Resident Withholding Tax (NRWT) on dividends and ordinary banking due diligence for source-of-funds verification. Capital repatriation via share buyback, capital reduction, or intercompany loan repayment may proceed without exchange control approval, although the Overseas Investment Act 2005 may apply only when the transaction crosses the 'significant business assets' threshold (generally NZD $100 million for non-Australian/non-US investors) or involves sensitive land.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: New Zealand imposes no statutory timeline, mandatory conversion ratio, or retention period for export proceeds. Export receipts from GDP pharma freight services may be retained in foreign currency, converted freely into NZD, or offset against offshore trade payables. The RBNZ collects balance-of-payments statistical data from registered banks, but this reporting is strictly statistical and does not limit currency choice, timing, onshore repatriation, or offshore retention of funds.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rated: High-Feasible with Constraints. Offshore fintech EMIs and digital payment institutions (e.g., Wise, Airwallex, Currencycloud) can provide low-cost multi-currency collection, SWIFT disbursement, and FX conversion for a low-risk GDP freight entity after remote onboarding with standard AML/KYC. However, they cannot fulfil statutory corporate banking requirements where a New Zealand-registered bank account is necessary for: (i) Inland Revenue tax payment obligations, (ii) NZD domestic ACH/BECS clearing through the Bulk Electronic Clearing System, (iii) documentary Letter of Credit operations under UCP600, or (iv) trust account / capital escrow functions. Legal constraints under the AML/CFT Act 2009 and the FMA e-money licensing framework require any EMI providing New Zealand-sourced services to residents to maintain a registered presence in NZ and to register as a reporting entity; offshore digital EMIs lacking a NZ-registered financial services provider licence are restricted to non-resident receivable collection and ancillary payments.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is permitted under the AML/CFT Act 2009 where a bank completes customer due diligence via certified electronic identity verification. In practice, all major NZ trading banks (ANZ, BNZ, ASB, Westpac) require at least one video-linked interview with the director(s) and each beneficial owner, plus certified passport, proof of residential address, and a wet-ink or digital-locked board resolution granting account authority. For a capital escrow account, an in-person or live video interview together with notarised board minutes and certified copies of constitutional documents are mandatory. Offshore directors are not required to travel to New Zealand if the bank accepts notarised identity packs certified at a New Zealand embassy or consulate, but remote opening without any interview is generally unavailable for a newly incorporated non-resident-owned NZ Ltd.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity through an offshore parent holding structure or nominee share arrangement
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Incorporation, New Zealand Companies Office extract, share register and ownership chart, trust deed and trustee resolution where relevant, signed beneficial ownership declaration, Independent Legal Advice (ILA) certificate, and stated capital injection plan supported by board minutes confirming the natural person ultimate beneficial owners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Lump-sum offshore capital injection without corroborating business history or prior freight transactions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Six months of corporate bank statements from the remitting bank, audited or certified management accounts, bank reference letter, loan agreement or shareholder capital resolution, executed trade invoices and signed GDP freight contracts, Medsafe GDP licence or compliance evidence, and a tax clearance certificate from the remitting jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pharmaceutical GDP freight entity screened as a latent higher-risk goods movement (cold-chain, dual-use cargo, or controlled substances)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Medsafe Good Distribution Practice (GDP) licence or statutory exemption, ISO 13485 quality management system certificate, Pharma GDP temperature-mapping qualification reports, endorsed shipping and cargo insurance documentation, counterparty due diligence list with sanctions-screening results, and a sworn declaration confirming non-exportation of controlled medicines without valid permits.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Director or shareholder PEP or sanctions-list name match
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: World-Check or Refinitiv screening output, sworn affidavit explaining the match and asserting no political or criminal nexus, source-of-wealth statement with supporting evidence (tax returns, property and asset valuations, certified corporate financial statements), and a covering legal opinion confirming no nexus to a sanctioned jurisdiction.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: (1) execute a board capital resolution and update the Companies Office share register; (2) remit via SWIFT MT103/MT202 from the investor's bank using purpose code 'CAPT' (Capital Contribution) or 'GFOA' (Goods/Freight Operating Advance) and include the NZ Ltd bank account and BIC (e.g., BNZENZ2L for BNZ); (3) tag the transfer as RBNZ balance-of-payments code 'Share Capital' or 'Intercompany Loan' — no exchange control approval is required; (4) confirm Overseas Investment Act 2005 nil-consent position because the capital injection funds an operating pharma freight entity below the significant business assets threshold and does not involve sensitive land; (5) deliver to the receiving bank the source-of-funds declaration, company resolution, and certified beneficial ownership register. The bank will tag the credit to the entity's 'Capital Suspense' for verification prior to release to the operating account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails: (a) SWIFT MT103 for direct supplier payments and freight settlement to USD/EUR/CAD payees; (b) Commercial Letter of Credit under UCP600 issued by the NZ commercial bank for offshore consignment purchases of pharmaceutical goods, including usance or 'red/blue clause' advances where contractually agreed; (c) Domestic NZD ACH/BECS disbursements through the Bulk Electronic Clearing System for local cold-chain logistics, storage, and customs clearance fees; and (d) on-behalf-of (OBO) structured SWIFT payments where the NZ Ltd funds a counterparty's account at a third-party bank for combined freight settlements. Every outbound transfer must include a correct RBNZ BOP transaction code (e.g., 'Freight Services' or 'Trade Credit'), pass sanctions and PEP screening, and be supported by the underlying invoice, packing list, bill of lading or air waybill, and GDP temperature record.

permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright Deliverable FX Forward (USD/NZD, EUR/NZD) for firm committed receivables and payables
Non-Deliverable Forward (NDF) available where the offshore counterparty requires a non-NZD settlement base, notwithstanding NZD full deliverability
Plain-Vanilla FX Options (OTC put/call on NZD) for contingent freight revenue hedging
Cross-Currency Swap (USD/NZD and EUR/NZD) for longer-dated intercompany loan or capital structure hedging
Rolling FX Forward Rollover / Tom-Next swaps for daily liquidity management

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return to the New Zealand Companies Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 9 months after the company's balance date; a standard 31 March balance date makes the annual return due by 31 December.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers late-filing notices and director-level fines under the Companies Act 1993; persistent non-filing, typically over two consecutive annual return periods, leads to the Registrar publishing a strike-off notice and removing the company from the Register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Financial Statements and Auditor's Report (for large companies and FMC reporting entities)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (filed with the Annual Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same statutory cycle as the Annual Return: no later than 9 months after balance date; for FMC reporting entities the Financial Markets Conduct Act filing timeframe applies.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to prepare and file required financial statements and the auditor's report is an offence under the Financial Reporting Act 2013 and Companies Act 1993; continuing default may result in fines, director prosecution, and administrative strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit applies to a New Zealand Ltd that is classified as 'large' under the Financial Reporting Act 2013 and XRB thresholds, including companies with total assets exceeding approximately NZ$60 million, annual revenue exceeding approximately NZ$30 million, or 50 or more full-time employees; FMC reporting entities also require statutory audit. Small and medium companies are audit-exempt unless required by the company's constitution or by shareholder resolution.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: NZ GAAP as established by the External Reporting Board: full NZ IFRS for large/publicly accountable companies; NZ IFRS Reduced Disclosure Regime for eligible smaller reporting entities; statutory foundation includes the Companies Act 1993 and Financial Reporting Act 2013.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand has no standalone annual public UBO filing for a private NZ Ltd. The Annual Return acts as the annual statutory confirmation of registered members and directors. Any share transfer must be recorded in the register of members before the transferee is registered; director and shareholder changes must be notified to the Companies Office within 20 working days. AML/CFT reporting entities in the freight/logistics sector must maintain current beneficial ownership records and, for higher-risk relationships, confirm UBO details at least annually.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000–18,000 depending on transaction volume, group structure, and large/small company status
